summary: The code is syntactically valid and includes many core data structures and helper functions, but it does not implement a runnable simulation. The main() function is empty, there is no simulation loop, critical behaviors (policy updates, retail interactions, enforcement, risk signaling, metrics collection) are not wired together, and several parameters are unused. The required direct call to main() is present.

issues.description: No runnable simulation: main() is empty and there is no simulation loop to orchestrate daily steps, update agents, retailers, locations, or collect metrics.
issues.solution: Implement a run() method in Simulation that iterates over days, updates risk signals, policies, enforcement, media effects, agent decisions, visits, retailer sales/restock, enforcement actions, and metrics. Instantiate and run Simulation in main().

issues.description: Location mask policies are never set to 'mandate' or 'recommended'; enforcement logic only triggers when mask_policy == 'mandate'.
issues.location: Simulation initialization and policy update flow
issues.solution: When HealthAuthority.mandate_on becomes True, set appropriate Location.mask_policy (e.g., for indoor_public types) and update enforcement levels via allocate_enforcement().

issues.description: Retailer and inventory logic is defined but unused. People do not purchase masks, retailer prices are never adjusted, restocks are not scheduled, and stockout metrics are not updated.
issues.solution: In daily loop, aggregate demand, attempt purchases from retailers respecting rationing and inventory, decrement person inventory on use, call adjust_prices(), and restock at restock_interval_days using supply_capacity_per_day. Track shortages and stockout_days.

issues.description: Risk signal parameters are defined but not applied to evolve risk_perception or observed conditions over time.
issues.solution: Implement a risk_signal(day) function using risk_signal_mode and risk_signal_period_days to update a global/public risk measure and incrementally adjust Person.risk_perception.

issues.description: Media and government guidance effects are not integrated into the simulation loop; InformationSource.broadcast_messages and HealthAuthority.issue_public_guidance are never invoked to update agents.
issues.solution: Each day, call authority.issue_public_guidance() and media.broadcast_messages(), combine signals by reach/credibility, and apply to a subset of agents (by media.reach) via Person.update_beliefs_from_media().

issues.description: Metrics scaffolding exists but is never populated beyond initialization. No adoption/compliance/churn calculations or per-location compliance aggregation.
issues.solution: Compute and append daily adoption_rate, compliance_over_time, churn (difference from previous day), update mask_shortage_incidents, enforcement_actions_count, denials_count, per-location compliance aggregates, and retailer_inventory_history during the daily loop.

issues.description: Person.decide_to_wear_mask uses enforcement_probability parameter without connecting it to actual visited locations’ enforcement levels; inventory is not decremented when using masks.
issues.solution: Compute enforcement probability based on visited locations’ enforcement levels and policies. When a person decides to wear a mask, decrement masks_inventory and optionally handle purchase replenishment.

issues.description: Parameter casting via int()/float() may raise ValueError if invalid types are provided; no validation or fallback handling.
issues.solution: Validate types and ranges for critical params, wrap casts with try/except, and clamp values or provide defaults on failure.

issues.description: Small-world rewiring builds candidate lists in O(n) per edge, which can be costly for large n.
issues.solution: Use rejection sampling with a bounded number of retries or maintain a precomputed list/bitset to sample new endpoints more efficiently.

issues.description: Several imports appear unused (json, csv, argparse, os, sys).
issues.solution: Remove unused imports unless they are required by the surrounding system; this reduces lint warnings and clarifies dependencies.
